Timestamp age and sequence position encode different assumptions. User-relative decay w(u,j)=exp[−λ(Tu−tuj)], with Tu the latest training timestamp, emphasizes each user’s recent behavior even when their history ends years ago. Global decay exp[−λ(T−tuj)], using a category-wide training cutoff T, additionally downweights users whose histories end earlier. Exactly, global weight equals user-relative weight times exp[−λ(T−Tu)]; per-user normalization therefore makes these exponential schemes identical. Sampled-window-position weighting measures event distance within a crop, ignores elapsed time, and can assign different weights to the same target across crops. Relevant research separates [temporal intervals](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.07382) from [recency-based target sampling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643).

Proposed controlled ablations: uniform weights; user-relative timestamp decay; global timestamp decay; full-history event-distance decay; sampled-window-position decay. Keep the GRU4Rec architecture, target/window draws, negatives, seeds, optimizer and training budget fixed. Compare within training-history-length, activity-rate and history-end-date strata; permute inter-event gaps within users and reconstruct timestamps to test whether actual gap placement adds value beyond event order. Log each target’s inclusion frequency, weighted user contribution and effective sample size. These controls distinguish temporal relevance from changes in user mass, gradient scale and sampling exposure; they are methodological proposals, not reported experimental findings.

For equal-user objectives, sample users uniformly and normalize target weights within each user. Normalize over the actual eligible-target distribution, accounting for truncation and repeated window inclusion. If targets are sampled with probability q(j|u), an unbiased estimator of a normalized desired target distribution p(j|u) uses p(j|u)/q(j|u), requiring nonzero support. Avoid applying decay through both sampling and loss unless that compounded objective is intentional. Batch self-normalization is generally biased; clipping trades variance for bias. Compute cutoffs, normalization constants and activity statistics exclusively from training histories.
